description: What Does a Positive Test Tell Us?; published open data from Pray et al. (2021), MMWR.
observation_unit: One paired nasal swab: an antigen-test swab and an RT-PCR swab collected from the same participant at the same visit. The 1,098 pairs include 57 participants tested on more than one day.
source: Published open data: Table 2 of Pray et al. (2021), Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report 69(51-52), Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; public domain.
publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report

citation.dataset: Pray, I. W., Ford, L., Cole, D., et al. (2021). Performance of an antigen-based test for asymptomatic and symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 testing at two university campuses - Wisconsin, September-October 2020. MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report, 69(51-52), 1642-1647. https://doi.org/10.15585/mmwr.mm695152a3

retrieved.version: MMWR 69(51-52), 1 January 2021; Table 2 read on the CDC page and on PMC, which agree. The CDC page notes that the report has been corrected; no erratum was found.

filters: Each of the eight Table 2 counts (symptom group by antigen result by RT-PCR result) becomes that many rows: asymptomatic first, then symptomatic, and within each group antigen+/PCR+, antigen+/PCR-, antigen-/PCR+, antigen-/PCR-.
specimen_pair_id numbers the 1,098 rows in that order; the report publishes counts, not records, so row order carries no information.
Results are coded 1 = positive and 0 = negative; symptomatic = 1 when one or more symptoms were reported at specimen collection.

columns.name: specimen_pair_id
columns.description: Label for one paired nasal swab, created when expanding the published table

columns.name: symptomatic
columns.description: Participant reported one or more COVID-19 symptoms at specimen collection

columns.name: antigen_positive
columns.description: Sofia SARS Antigen Fluorescent Immunoassay result

columns.name: pcr_positive
columns.description: Real-time RT-PCR result, the study's reference standard
